claims.claim_text: GPTZero's Hallucination Detector is designed to automatically detect hallucinated sources and poorly supported claims in essays.
claims.evidence_span: GPTZero's Hallucination Detector automatically detects hallucinated sources and poorly supported claims in essays.

claims.claim_text: GPTZero citation checker identifies hallucinated references instantly to help educators maintain academic integrity.
claims.evidence_span: Our citation checker identifies these hallucinated references instantly, helping educators maintain academic integrity without spending time on manual verification.

claims.claim_text: GPTZero source finder detects checkable, objective claims in text and matches those to sources from online, academic, and publicly available data.
claims.evidence_span: Source finder will detect as many checkable, objective claims in your text and match those to sources from online, academic, and publicly available data coming from AI-powered search engines.

claims.claim_text: An artificial intelligence hallucination is defined as a response generated by AI that contains false or misleading information presented as fact.
claims.evidence_span: In the field of artificial intelligence (AI), a hallucination or artificial hallucination (also called bullshitting, confabulation, delusion, or mirage) is a response generated by AI that contains false or misleading information presented as fact.

claims.claim_text: In July 2021, Meta warned that BlenderBot 2 was prone to hallucinations defined as confident statements that are not true.
claims.evidence_span: In July 2021, Meta warned during its release of BlenderBot 2 that the system is prone to hallucinations, defined as confident statements that are not true.

claims.claim_text: In 2023, the Cambridge dictionary updated its definition of hallucination to include the new sense specific to the field of AI.
claims.evidence_span: In 2023, the Cambridge dictionary updated its definition of hallucination to include this new sense specific to the field of AI.

claims.claim_text: The survey paper covers major detection and verification paradigms including retrieval-augmented generation, factuality evaluation metrics, and automated fact-checking.
claims.evidence_span: Subsequently, we examine major detection and verification paradigms, including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), factuality evaluation metrics, automated fact-checking, natural language inference (NLI), knowledge-grounded reasoning, multi-model verification, and self-reflection-based approaches.

claims.claim_text: AI hallucinations are defined as instances where an AI system produces outputs that sound plausible but are factually wrong, irrelevant or entirely fabricated.
claims.evidence_span: AI hallucinations are instances where an AI system produces outputs that sound plausible but are factually wrong, irrelevant or entirely fabricated.

claims.claim_text: Factual hallucinations occur when an AI tool states information that is objectively false about the world.
claims.evidence_span: Factual hallucinations occur when an AI tool states information that is objectively false about the world.

claims.claim_text: Contextual hallucinations happen when the AI is supposed to answer a prompt by using specific contextual data but instead relies on its general training data.
claims.evidence_span: Contextual hallucinations happen when the AI is supposed to answer a prompt by using specific contextual data, such as a document or database, but instead relies on its general training data.

claims.claim_text: Consistency hallucinations occur when an AI model contradicts itself within the same conversation.
claims.evidence_span: Consistency hallucinations occur when an AI model contradicts itself within the same conversation.

claims.claim_text: An artificial intelligence hallucination is when a language model produces content that sounds authoritative and well-reasoned but is factually wrong or entirely made up.
claims.evidence_span: An AI hallucination is when a language model produces content that sounds authoritative and well-reasoned but is factually wrong or entirely made up.

claims.claim_text: Stanford research found that even specialized legal AI tools hallucinate between 17% and 34% of the time.
claims.evidence_span: Stanford research found that even specialized legal AI tools hallucinate between 17% and 34% of the time.

claims.claim_text: A 2024 Stanford study found that combining Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback, and guardrails led to a 96% reduction in hallucinations.
claims.evidence_span: A 2024 Stanford study found that combining Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), and guardrails led to a 96% reduction in hallucinations.
